class.name: JarNoise
class.brief_description: Fractal noise for terrain, with exact gradients.
class.description: 3D simplex noise that returns its exact gradient along with the value, so terrain slopes cost no extra samples. Fractals: [constant FRACTAL_FBM] (rolling, natural detail) or [constant FRACTAL_RIDGED] (sharp, branching crests for mountain ranges), with an optional domain warp that bends the shapes into more natural, less grid-like forms. It runs inside the extension, with no engine call per sample. [JarTerrainSdf] takes it for any of its noises; with [JarNoise] throughout it builds terrain about twice as fast as with [FastNoiseLite], and its distances and normals are more accurate. Values are in about [-1, 1]. Gradients are per unit of input (per meter for positions in meters), frequency included. 2D sampling reads the XZ plane of the 3D noise.

members.member: How octaves combine: [constant FRACTAL_NONE], [constant FRACTAL_FBM] or [constant FRACTAL_RIDGED].
Frequency of the first octave: 1 / its feature size, in cycles per unit (per meter).
Amplitude of each octave relative to the previous one. Lower values give smoother noise.
Frequency of each octave relative to the previous one.
Number of octaves (ignored with [constant FRACTAL_NONE]). Each costs one simplex sample.
Frequency of the domain warp's own noise. Lower than [member frequency] bends whole features; higher roughens them.

How far, in input units (meters), the input position is pushed around before sampling: 0 turns the warp off. It costs three more simplex samples. Keep [member warp_strength] * [member warp_frequency] well below 1, or features fold over themselves.

constants.constant: Octaves summed (fractal Brownian motion): rolling, natural detail.
Per octave 1 - |n|, squared: sharp crests along the noise's zero lines, branching like mountain ridges. The crests are rounded off very slightly, so the gradient stays continuous.
